overview.description: Scopa Corse is the Corsican variant of Scopa, played with a 36-card Italian deck (no 2s). Players capture table cards by matching rank or by sum; unlike basic Scopa, capturing is optional. First to 21 points wins.

history.origins: Scopa originated in Italy and was especially popular in Naples by the 18th century; it spread to Corsica where it is played as Scopa Corse with a 36-card deck (twos removed) and optional capture. The Corsican form is played alongside related games in Spain and North Africa and is documented with EREDI-brand rules; the stripped deck adds tactical depth by making sums of 7 harder to form.
timeline: 20th century: Corsican variant of Scopa documented with 36-card deck and optional capture; rules published with EREDI brand cards.

setup.deck: 36-card Italian deck: each suit has Ace, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, Jack, Queen, King (no 2s).
setup.dealing: 3 cards to each player, 4 face-up on the table. Two players: next three deals 3 cards each, last two deals 4 cards each. Four players: second deal 3 each, third deal 2 each.

rules.objective: Capture cards from the table by playing a card that matches a single table card or the sum of a set; score for most cards, most coins, settebello, primiera, and sweeps. First to 21 points wins.
rules.gameplay: Players take turns playing one card. The played card may capture one card of equal value, or a set of table cards whose values sum to the played card's value. In Scopa Corse capturing is optional: a player may leave a card on the table even if it could capture. Clearing the table scores a scopa (1 point). After each round of plays, new cards are dealt. Play and scoring otherwise match basic Scopa.
keyRules: Target score usually 21; may be 16 or 11 by agreement.

strategy.basic: Prioritize sweeps when useful; use optional capture to avoid leaving combinations for the opponent. Track coins and primiera.
tips: Without 2s, forming sums of 7 is harder; use that to plan when to leave cards on the table.

edgeCases.text: In Scopa Corse capturing is optional; a player may play a card and leave it on the table without capturing even if a match or sum exists.
If the played card matches both a single table card and a set summing to its value, the single card must be captured, not the set.

engine.deckDescription: A 36-card Italian deck used in Corsica for Scopa Corse: four suits (Cups, Coins, Swords, Batons), each with Ace, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, Jack, Queen, King. The twos are removed.
engine.suitDescription: Italian suits used in Scopa Corse: coins (denari), cups (coppe), swords (spade), and batons (bastoni). Each suit has nine cards in this game; the same four suits appear in the 40-card Italian deck but here the twos are removed.
engine.rankDescription: Stripped 36: Ace, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, Jack, Queen, King in each suit; no 2s.
engine.dealPattern: 3,3,3,3,4,4 for two players; 3,3,2 for four players

scoring.description: As basic Scopa: 1 point per scopa (sweep), 1 for most cards, 1 for most coins, 1 for settebello (7 of coins), 1 for best primiera.
scoring.winCondition: First player or team to reach the target score (usually 21) wins.
